column3: Strongest evidence: matches experiment, or the deciding source is >=90% likely to be within 2 kcal/mol.
Good evidence: the source is >=70% likely to be within 2 kcal/mol, or a second source corroborates it.
Weakest evidence: below 70% likely, or contradicted by the other sources.
Checked directly against an experimental value. Overrides everything else.
At least 90% likely to land within 2 kcal/mol of the truth.
At least 70% likely to land within 2 kcal/mol.
Below 70% likely. Most reactions sit here.
Another source agrees, within both their error bars. Can lift bronze to silver, never to gold.
The other sources disagree by more than their error bars allow, and this one is the outlier. Costs a tier.
Only one source scored this reaction, so no cross-check was possible.
A cross-check ran and settled neither way - it neither helped nor penalised.
An experimental measurement from the NIST thermodynamics database.
